When he is satisfied, Viśveśa is indeed satisfied; there is no doubt about this. Wherever this section, which is the refuge of supreme bliss, is recited, no source of inauspiciousness can prevail there.
The wise man who hears this, and the intelligent person who causes this to be heard; || 123 ||
Even those meritorious souls who merely recite this, they are all forms of Rudra;
and he who, having had this beautiful book transcribed, should offer it [to a temple], [attains the same]. 124.
By him all the Purāṇas have been given, and not otherwise; for however many narratives are here, however many verses indeed,
as many words, and as many letters as there are— 125.
And however many syllables there may be, and however many lines of verse there may be; || 126 ||
As many threads as there are in the strands, as many warp-threads as there are in the cloth, and as many variegated forms as there are upon the beautiful surface of the book.
For that many thousands of yugas, the donor is glorified in heaven;
he who hears this supreme section twelve times [attains the same].
Even the sin of killing a Brahmin shall quickly perish for him through the grace of Śambhu.
Furthermore, if one who is childless listens [to this] while well-bathed and endowed with faith,

What is the use of saying more? Whatever desire anyone may have here, that virtuous person shall always attain it upon hearing this.
Whoever hears this excellent Kāśīkhaṇḍa, even from a distant land, shall, by the command of Śiva, become a recipient of the merit of residing in Kāśī. 131.
From hearing this, men shall achieve victory everywhere;
moreover, one whose heart is pure shall attain good fortune in all places.
Only for him with whom Viśveśvara is pleased does the inclination to hear this arise.
It arises for one endowed with merit and a greatly pure mind.
It is the supreme and greatest of all auspicious things;
even when written in the home, it is to be worshipped for the attainment of all auspiciousness. || 133-134 ||

Salutation to Kṛṣṇa, to Hari, the sole sun filled with the mass of existence, consciousness, and bliss, who assumes a body according to the desires of his devotees.
In Vedānta he was like Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī; in Sunaya, like Bhārgava; in the Nyāya system, like Gautama Akṣapāda, who is even more venerable than Kaṇāda;
in Sāṃkhya, like Kapila, the son of Devahūtī; and likewise in the Yoga-śāstra, he was like Vāsuki.
In the first chapter, may that supreme teacher, the illustrious Surendra, who is equal to Bhaṭṭa, be victorious for us. || 2 ||
In the Vedānta, he is the son of Śrī Satyavatī; in the system of the Purāṇas and the Mahābhārata, he is Śrī Kapila; in Sāṃkhya, he is Kaṇāda; here in Vaiśeṣika, he is Gautama;
in Nyāya, he is Patañjali; and in the system of Yoga, he is Candraprabhāvallabha.
Victorious is Bhaṭṭācārya Caturbhuja, who is a pre-eminent follower of Kumārila. I have written two commentaries, one with a treasury [of examples] and one without;
whichever of them one has a desire for, let that be accepted by him.
There was a venerable Brahmin, a jewel who adorned the lineage of Kaśyapa, beloved of Mukunda,
a son of the noble Gadādhara, clad in white garments and possessed of excellent intellect;
from him, a son named Śrīrāma was born from the womb of Gandharvī.
This commentary, composed by Śrī Stenarāja for the benefit of the learned, should be examined by the wise. || 5 ||
In Kāśī, by the learned and pure-souled Bhaṭṭa Śrī Puruṣottama, who knows the Tantras, Ādhyātma Purāṇas, and the Mahābhārata, and who worships the enemy of Kaṃsa (Kṛṣṇa);
together with the commentary of profound meaning composed by the eminent sage Rāmānanda.
This great *Śrī-Kāśīkhaṇḍa* has been correctly compiled for the benefit of the wise.

Thus ends the one hundredth chapter in the commentary on the *Kāśīkhaṇḍa*, composed by Rāmānanda—also known as Caitanyavana—who is a disciple of the venerable Śrī Rāmendravana, himself a disciple of the holy and worshipful Paramahaṃsa Parivrājaka Ācārya. 100.
And this commentary on the Kāśīkhaṇḍa is completed.
Dohā—This *Kāśī-khaṇḍa* is purifying; it increases the growth of auspiciousness.
